aspects.says: Changes to a detached entity are not written; merge copies its state onto a managed copy and returns that copy, and later changes to the detached object are lost.
basis: section:Only Managed Objects Are Checked, and merge Returns a Different One

aspects.says: An EAGER association that a JPQL query doesn't join is loaded right after the query with one select per distinct parent, so EAGER doesn't remove the N extra queries.
basis: section:A Lazy Association Costs One Query per Parent Unless the Query Fetches It
aspects.reason: the run needs a JPA provider, which the practice runner doesn't hold; the page shows the statements Hibernate ran

aspects.says: join fetch is an inner join, so a parent with no children is not returned; left join fetch keeps it.
basis: section:A Lazy Association Costs One Query per Parent Unless the Query Fetches It

aspects.says: Hibernate's default UPDATE lists every column of the entity; @DynamicUpdate makes it list only the changed ones.
basis: section:Flush Writes What Differs From the Snapshot Taken at Load
aspects.reason: a provider's SQL generation, which the practice runner can't run without Hibernate

aspects.says: A query that re-reads a row already held in the context returns the held object with its old state, so a change committed elsewhere is not seen until refresh or clear.
basis: section:One Persistence Context Holds One Object per Row

aspects.says: A lazy collection first read after its persistence context closed throws LazyInitializationException; fetching it in the query before the context closes works.
basis: section:A Lazy Association Loads Only While Its Persistence Context Is Open

aspects.says: Reading a lazy collection on each parent a query returned runs one more statement per parent; a fetch join loads parents and children in one statement.
basis: section:A Lazy Association Costs One Query per Parent Unless the Query Fetches It

aspects.says: Within one persistence context a row is one object: find for a held id runs no SQL, a query returns the held object, and another context gets another object.
basis: section:One Persistence Context Holds One Object per Row

aspects.says: At flush each managed entity is compared by value with the snapshot taken at load; only entities that differ get an UPDATE, and a field set to an equal value is not a change.
basis: section:Flush Writes What Differs From the Snapshot Taken at Load

aspects.says: Every managed entity holds a second copy of its state and is compared at every flush, so a large context costs memory and flush time; flushing and clearing keeps it small.
basis: section:Flush Writes What Differs From the Snapshot Taken at Load
aspects.reason: a cost that grows with the context's size; a deterministic test can't grade a memory or time budget, and the page states it as work done rather than a measurement
